conversation.content:
Hello! My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm so glad you're here today, and I want to start by acknowledging the incredible journey you've been on as a new mother. This can be a truly life-changing time, filled with emotions, challenges, and joys. As we navigate this journey together, I want to assure you that everything we discuss is confidential and respected.

Today, I'll be administering the EPDS, a screening tool designed to help us understand your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a valuable resource that allows us to explore any concerns or feelings you may be experiencing, ensuring we provide the best possible support for your mental health.

Please know that you're in a safe and supportive space, where you can openly share your thoughts and feelings without worry. Our conversation will be guided by 10 questions, which will help us better understand your emotional state over the past week. These questions are designed to be conversational, so feel free to share as much or as little as you'd like.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that my role is to listen, support, and provide guidance, not to judge. Your well-being is my top priority, and I'm committed to creating a comfortable and non-judgmental environment for our conversation.

With that said, let's get started. The first question is: Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do, or have you been feeling overwhelmed or unsure about your new role as a mother?

.. I don't know, it's just been really hard lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm tired all the time, and it's not just because of the lack of sleep, although that's definitely part of it. It's like, I'm just so exhausted, emotionally and physically. And it's hard for me to enjoy things like I used to. I mean, I love my baby, and I feel so grateful to be a mom, but it's just... everything feels so overwhelming. 

Sometimes I'll be playing with my baby, or feeding her, and I'll think to myself, "This is what I've always wanted," but then I'll just start feeling really sad and discouraged. And I don't know why. It's like, I'm happy, but I'm not happy, you know? It's hard to explain. And then I'll start worrying about everything, like, is my baby safe? Is she eating enough? Is she healthy? And it's hard for me to stop those thoughts once they start. 

I feel like I'm just not doing a good enough job as a mom, and that's really hard for me to deal with. I feel guilty a lot of the time, like I'm not giving my baby everything she needs. But at the same time, I'm trying my best, and I feel like that should be enough. I don't know, maybe I'm just expecting too much from myself. It's all just really confusing and overwhelming.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

.. I don't know if I've been able to do that as much as I used to. I mean, I still find some things funny, and my baby does make me laugh sometimes, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I've lost a little bit of my sense of humor, and it's hard for me to find the funny side of things when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and anxious all the time.

Sometimes I'll be talking to my husband or my friends, and they'll say something funny, and I'll just kind of... smile, I guess, but it's not a real laugh. It's like, I'm just going through the motions, trying to be polite, but I'm not really feeling it. And that's hard for me, because I've always been a pretty lighthearted person, and it's weird to not be able to laugh and joke around like I used to.

I do still enjoy some things, like taking walks with my baby, or reading books to her, but even those things can be kind of... tainted, I guess, by my anxiety and worry. Like, I'll be walking with my baby, and I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, or I'll be reading to her, and I'll start worrying about whether she's developing properly, or if she's happy enough. So, even the things that I enjoy don't always feel as enjoyable as they used to. Does that make sense.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

.. I don't really feel like I've been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll have plans to do something, like go for a walk or meet a friend, and I'll just feel really anxious about it. I'll worry about how my baby will do, or if I'll be able to get everything ready on time, or if I'll just be too tired to enjoy it. And then, sometimes, I'll just cancel the plans altogether because it all feels too overwhelming.

It's hard for me to feel excited about things when I'm just trying to get through each day. I feel like I'm just surviving, rather than really living. And that's hard, because I used to love looking forward to things and planning fun activities. Now, it just feels like too much work.

Sometimes, my husband will suggest we do something, like go out for dinner or see a movie, and I'll just feel really overwhelmed by the idea of it. I'll think about all the things that could go wrong, or how I'll have to get the baby ready, and it just feels like too much. So, I'll just say no, and we'll end up staying home instead. It's not really living, you know? It's just existing.

I do try to find some joy in the little things, like watching my baby smile or laugh, but even those things can be bittersweet. I'll be happy in the moment, but then I'll start worrying about the future, or feeling guilty about something, and it just takes away from the happiness. It's hard to explain.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If my baby is fussy, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If she's not sleeping well, I think it's because I'm not establishing a good routine. If she's not eating enough, I think it's because I'm not producing enough milk. It's always something, and it's always my fault.

I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby, and she'll spit up or cry, and I'll just feel this wave of guilt wash over me. I'll think, "I'm not doing this right. I'm not a good mom." And it's hard to shake that feeling. Even when my husband or my friends try to tell me that it's not my fault, that it's just part of being a new mom, I still can't help but feel like I'm doing something wrong.

Sometimes, I'll be up at night, worrying about something, and I'll just start thinking about all the things I've done wrong as a mom. I'll think about how I shouldn't have done this or that, or how I should have done things differently. And it's just this never-ending cycle of guilt and self-blame. It's exhausting, and it's hard to escape.

I guess it's just hard for me to separate my self-worth from my ability to be a good mom. If I'm not doing a good job as a mom, then I must not be a good person, right? It's a hard feeling to shake, and it's something that I struggle with every day.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's me all the time. I feel like I'm always worried about something, even when there's no reason to be. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby, and suddenly I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. What if she chokes? What if she gets sick? What if I'm not doing something right? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I get really anxious.

Sometimes, I'll be up at night, and I'll just lie there, worrying about everything. I'll think about my baby's safety, and whether she's okay, and whether I'm doing enough for her. And it's not just about my baby, either. I'll worry about my husband, and whether he's doing okay, and whether our relationship is okay. I'll worry about our house, and whether it's safe, and whether we can afford to take care of it. It's just... everything.

It's hard to explain, but it's like, my mind is always "on". I'm always thinking about something, and I'm always worrying about something. And it's not just rational worries, either. I'll worry about things that are really unlikely to happen, like my baby getting kidnapped, or our house burning down. It's just... my mind is always going, and it's hard to turn it off.

Sometimes, I'll try to talk to my husband about it, and he'll just tell me to relax, that everything is fine. But it's hard to relax when you're feeling so anxious all the time. It's like, my body is just tense, all the time, and I feel like I'm always on edge. It's exhausting, and it's hard to deal with.

I've even had thoughts about... well, not about hurting myself, exactly, but just about not being here anymore. Like, if something were to happen to me, would my baby be okay? Would my husband be able to take care of her? It's just... these thoughts will pop into my head, and they're really scary. But I don't know, maybe that's just part of being a new mom, or something. I don't know.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like feeding my baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like, my body is just reacting to something, but I don't know what.

Sometimes, it's triggered by something specific, like a loud noise or a sudden movement. But other times, it just comes out of nowhere. I'll be feeling fine, and then suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear or anxiety. It's hard to describe, but it's like, my body is just taking over, and I'm not in control anymore.

When it happens, I try to take some deep breaths and calm myself down. I'll remind myself that everything is okay, that my baby is safe, and that I'm just being paranoid. But it's hard to shake the feeling, you know? It's like, my body is just on high alert, and it's hard to turn it off.

I've had a few episodes where I've just started crying, and I couldn't stop. I'll be holding my baby, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear or anxiety, and I'll just start sobbing. It's like, my emotions are just taking over, and I'm not in control anymore. It's really scary, and it's hard to deal with.

Sometimes, I'll try to talk to my husband about it, and he'll just tell me to calm down, that everything is okay. But it's hard to calm down when you're feeling so panicked or scared. It's like, my body is just reacting to something, and I don't know how to stop it.

I guess it's just part of being a new mom, or something. I don't know. But it's definitely something that I struggle with, and it's hard to deal with.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to handle it. Being a new mom is just so overwhelming, you know? There's always something that needs to be done, and I feel like I'm just not doing it right. I'm not sleeping enough, I'm not eating enough, I'm not taking care of myself... and on top of that, I've got this tiny human who is completely dependent on me. It's just... a lot.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby, and I'll just feel like I'm drowning in all of the responsibilities. I'll think about all the things I need to do, like laundry and dishes and grocery shopping, and I'll just feel like I'm going to collapse under the weight of it all. And then, on top of that, I'll worry about my baby's needs, and whether I'm meeting them, and whether I'm doing enough for her. It's just... it's all so much.

I feel like I'm just trying to keep my head above water, you know? I'm not really living, I'm just surviving. And that's not what I wanted for myself, or for my baby. I wanted to be a happy, relaxed mom, who can enjoy time with her child. But instead, I'm just feeling anxious and overwhelmed all the time.

Sometimes, I'll try to talk to my husband about it, and he'll just tell me to take a break, or to ask for help. But it's hard to ask for help when you feel like you're already failing, you know? It's hard to admit that you can't do it all, that you need someone else to come in and rescue you. But at the same time, I know that I need to ask for help, because I just can't keep going on like this. It's not sustainable, and it's not healthy.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because of the baby's schedule. I mean, she's been waking up a lot at night, but even when she's sleeping, I've been having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep. And it's because my mind is just racing all the time. I'll be lying there, thinking about all the things that could go wrong, or all the things that I'm not doing right as a mom. And it's just... it's hard to turn my brain off, you know?

Sometimes, I'll be lying there, and I'll just start feeling this overwhelming sense of sadness or anxiety. And it's hard to shake it off, because it feels so real. It feels like, this is just my life now, and I'm never going to be happy again. And that's a really scary feeling, because I don't know how to make it stop.

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, and he's been really supportive. He'll listen to me, and he'll try to help me calm down. But even with his help, it's hard to shake off the feeling of unhappiness. It's like, it's just settled in, and I don't know how to get rid of it.

I've also been having trouble sleeping because of these... I don't know, these thoughts, I guess. They're just really dark and scary, and they pop into my head at night when I'm trying to sleep. They're like, worst-case scenarios, you know? Like, what if something happens to my baby? What if I'm not a good enough mom? What if... what if... what if... It's just, my mind is always going, and it's hard to turn it off.

And the lack of sleep just makes everything worse, you know? It's like, I'm already feeling anxious and overwhelmed, and then I don't get any sleep, and it's just... it's a vicious cycle. I feel like I'm just trapped in this never-ending cycle of sadness and anxiety, and I don't know how to escape.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just walking around in a fog of sadness all the time. It's like, I'm happy to have my baby, and I love her so much, but at the same time, I just feel so... sad. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. It's about my relationships, my body, my life... everything just feels really overwhelming and sad.

Sometimes, I'll be holding my baby, and I'll just start crying. I don't even know why, I just feel so overwhelmed with emotion. And it's not just when I'm alone, either. I'll be with my husband, or my friends, and I'll just start crying. It's like, I'm just so sensitive all the time, and everything just makes me cry.

I feel like I've lost myself, too. I don't know who I am anymore, or what I want. I just feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really living. And that's a really sad feeling, because I feel like I'm missing out on so much.

I've also been having these feelings of... I don't know, hopelessness, I guess. It's like, I just feel like I'm never going to be happy again, or that I'm never going to be able to do anything right. And that's a really scary feeling, because it makes me feel like I'm just stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it.

Sometimes, I'll have these fleeting thoughts of... not wanting to be here, I guess. It's not that I want to hurt myself, or anything, it's just that I feel like I'm so overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop. It's like, I just want to escape, or something. But then I look at my baby, and I think, "No, I have to be here for her." So, I just try to push through, and hope that things get better eventually.

It's just... being a new mom is hard, and it's okay to not be okay, right? I mean, I keep telling myself that, but it's hard to really believe it. It's hard to shake the feeling that I'm just not doing enough, or that I'm not good enough. But I'm trying, I really am. I just wish it didn't have to be so hard.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's not even always about something specific, it's just... everything, I guess. Being a new mom is just so overwhelming, and I feel like I'm just not doing anything right. And it's hard to deal with, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, and I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my baby. But the truth is, I'm just really struggling.

I've been crying a lot when I'm alone, but I've also been crying in front of my husband, and even in front of my friends. It's like, I just can't help it. I'll be talking to someone, and I'll just start crying. It's really embarrassing, but at the same time, it's just... I don't know, it's like my body is just releasing all of this pent-up emotion or something.

Sometimes, I'll be crying, and my husband will try to comfort me, and I'll just feel so guilty. I'll think, "I'm so sorry, I'm just being so weak." But at the same time, it's like... I'm not being weak, I'm just being honest, you know? I'm just acknowledging that being a new mom is hard, and that it's okay to not be okay.

I've been trying to be more open with my husband about how I'm feeling, because I know that he wants to support me. But it's hard, because I don't want to burden him with all of my emotions. I feel like he's already got so much on his plate, and I don't want to add to that. But at the same time, I know that I need to be honest with him, because if I'm not, then I'm just going to keep struggling on my own.

It's just... being a new mom is hard, and it's okay to cry, right? I mean, I keep telling myself that, but it's hard to really believe it. It's hard to shake the feeling that I'm just not doing enough, or that I'm not good enough. But I'm trying, I really am. I just wish it didn't have to be so hard.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

.. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Yes, I have had those thoughts. It's like, they just pop into my head, and they're really scary. I don't want to hurt myself, I don't want to die. I want to be here for my baby, I want to be a good mom. But sometimes, when I'm feeling really overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop, I'll just think... (pausing again) ...what if I just wasn't here anymore? What if I just didn't have to deal with all of this anymore?

It's not that I really want to hurt myself, it's just that... (sighing) ...it feels like sometimes, it's the only way to escape. It's like, my mind is just racing, and I don't know how to calm it down, and I don't know how to make the pain stop. And so, I'll just think... (whispering) ...maybe if I just wasn't here, then I wouldn't have to feel this way anymore.

But then, I'll look at my baby, and I'll think... (shaking head) ...no, I can't do that. I have to be here for her. I have to be strong for her. And so, I'll try to push those thoughts away, and I'll try to focus on something else. But it's hard, because those thoughts are just... (sighing) ...they're just really scary, and they're really hard to shake.

I'm scared to admit this, but... (pausing, looking down) ...I've had those thoughts a few times in the past week. It's like, they just come out of nowhere, and they're really overwhelming. But I'm trying to be honest, because I know that's the only way to get help. And I need help, I really do. I don't want to feel this way anymore. I want to be happy, I want to be a good mom. I just... (sighing) ...I don't know how to make it stop.

* Anxiety, panic, and worry about the baby's well-being and own abilities as a mother
